olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: (a) Suppose each square of a $4\times 7$ board is colored black or white. Prove that the board must contain a rectangle whose four corner squares are all the same color. (b) Exhibit a coloring of a $4\times 6$ board where no such rectangle exists.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1976

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: If $A$ and $B$ are fixed points on a given circle and $XY$ is a variable diameter, determine the locus of the intersection of lines $AX$ and $BY$. (Assume $AB$ is not a diameter.)
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1976

source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1976

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: If the sum of the lengths of the six edges of a trirectangular tetrahedron $PABC$ (i.e., $\angle APB=\angle BPC=\angle CPA=90^\circ$) is $S$, determine its maximum volume.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1976

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: If $P(x),Q(x),R(x),S(x)$ are polynomials such that $P(x^5)+xQ(x^5)+x^2R(x^5)=(x^4+x^3+x^2+x+1)S(x)$, prove that $x-1$ is a factor of $P(x)$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1976
